title: You can now call out LinkedIn AI slop using a new button
excerpt: LinkedIn now allows users to flag "AI slop" in their feeds as it seeks to crack down on a wave of low quality, AI-generated posts.
content_html:
Is your LinkedIn feed filthy with AI slop? Have you read enough generic ChatGPT broetry to make you want to log off and open a real book?

LinkedIn has a solution.

The company is introducing a new feature this week that lets users flag when a post in their feed "seems like AI slop."

When you tag a post as sloppy, it will disappear from your feed. LinkedIn is also testing a method of privately notifying the poster in their account dashboard that their words "may have come off as inauthentic," according to the company's chief product officer, Hari Srinivasan, who wrote about the feature on Thursday.

The company doesn't want to be the arbiter of what is good or bad AI content, he said, because "AI and slop are not the same thing."

"We want members to get feedback from real humans on what sounds authentic — not just have an AI detector review it and get it wrong," he continued.

AI-generated content has run rampant on LinkedIn in recent months. Like its social-network peers TikTok and Instagram, the company is reckoning with a wave of artificially made posts as generative AI tools like Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's ChatGPT, and ByteDance's Seedance 2.0 make it much easier to spin up content quickly.

LinkedIn has developed its own particular brand of AI slop, as corporate leaders, entrepreneurs, and job hunters flood the feed with generic, AI-generated thought leadership and business truisms. The AI detector company Pangram recently estimated that 41% of long LinkedIn posts and 30% of shorter posts were AI-generated.

Other media platforms have been testing ways to cut down on poorly written AI content. The newsletter app Substack recently announced a partnership with Pangram to let users scan for AI, for example. In November, TikTok began testing the ability to let users toggle how much AI content appears in their feeds.

Cracking down on unwanted AI could be critical for the platforms as they look to avoid alienating users.

"AI slop is a top priority for all of us," Srinivasan wrote in his post. "We really care about this. People come to LinkedIn to connect with real people and share their real perspectives, ideas and expertise."

content_html_zh:
您的 LinkedIn feed 是否充斥着 AI 垃圾？ 您是否读过足够多的通用 ChatGPT 文章，让您想要注销并打开一本真正的书？

LinkedIn 有一个解决方案。

该公司本周推出了一项新功能，可以让用户在提要中的帖子“看起来像人工智能失控”时进行标记。

当您将帖子标记为马虎时，它就会从您的源中消失。 LinkedIn 还在测试一种方法，可以在其帐户仪表板上私下通知发帖者，他们的言论“可能被认为不真实”，该公司首席产品官 Hari Srinivasan 周四撰文介绍了该功能。

他说，该公司不想成为人工智能内容好坏的仲裁者，因为“人工智能和垃圾不是一回事。”

“我们希望会员能够从真实的人类那里获得关于听起来真实的反馈——而不仅仅是让人工智能探测器对其进行审查并出错，”他继续说道。

近几个月来，人工智能生成的内容在 LinkedIn 上泛滥成灾。 与社交网络同行 TikTok 和 Instagram 一样，该公司正在应对一波人工发布的帖子，因为 Anthropic 的 Claude、OpenAI 的 ChatGPT 和 ByteDance 的 Seedance 2.0 等生成人工智能工具使快速生成内容变得更加容易。

随着企业领导者、企业家和求职者充斥着通用的、人工智能生成的思想领导力和商业真理，LinkedIn 已经开发出了自己独特的人工智能品牌。 AI 探测器公司 Pangram 最近估计，LinkedIn 41% 的长帖子和 30% 的短帖子是 AI 生成的。

其他媒体平台一直在测试减少编写质量不佳的人工智能内容的方法。 例如，时事通讯应用程序 Substack 最近宣布与 Pangram 合作，让用户可以扫描 AI。 11 月，TikTok 开始测试让用户切换其信息流中出现多少人工智能内容的功能。

打击不需要的人工智能对于平台来说至关重要，因为它们希望避免疏远用户。

“人工智能问题是我们所有人的首要任务，”斯里尼瓦桑在他的帖子中写道。 “我们真的很关心这个。 人们来到 LinkedIn 是为了与真实的人联系并分享他们的真实观点、想法和专业知识。”
